docs.text:
These adaptations use mineru -p, mineru-api, mineru-gradio, and mineru-models-download, not 4.0 mineru-kit. Legacy references:

  • 3.4.5 installation
  • 3.4.5 model configuration

Vendors control prebuilt image contents; a <4 bound in this repository does not modify existing images. Check inside the container before deployment:

python -c "from importlib.metadata import version; from packaging.specifiers import SpecifierSet; v = version('mineru'); print(v); assert v in SpecifierSet('<4'), 'Use the vendor image for MinerU <4'"

docs.title: file-parse API: Synchronous Single-File Parsing
docs.text: This page describes the 4.1.0 interface. mineru-kit file-parse-server is a standalone HTTP wrapper: it accepts one file, creates and uploads a Task, waits, and returns a ZIP, DOCX, or HTML attachment. It connects to a local API, Router, or compatible SaaS without loading parsing models.

docs.title: Startup
docs.text:
Start the upstream parser, then start the wrapper in another terminal:

mineru-kit api-server --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --tier auto

mineru-kit file-parse-server --api-url http://127.0.0.1:8000
Option Default Meaning --api-url MINERU_API_URL, otherwise required Upstream API base, optionally with a proxy prefix; do not append /v1/tasks. --api-key MINERU_API_KEY, otherwise empty Bearer token for upstream requests only. --host, --port 127.0.0.1, 8003 Wrapper listen address. --state-dir ${MINERU_HOME:-~/.mineru}/file-parse Recovery database and temporary transfer directory. --retention-seconds 86400 Record retention after first observing a terminal state; 0 disables collection.

The wrapper has no API-key authentication of its own and is intended for local or trusted-network use. Add authentication at a reverse proxy when exposing it externally. Incoming Authorization is not forwarded upstream; requests cannot override the upstream address or credentials.

The wrapper has its own /docs and /openapi.json. The routes below exist only on this service, not on the main API Server or Router.

docs.title: Request fields
docs.text:
POST /v1/file_parse accepts only multipart/form-data. Query parameters, unknown fields, multiple files, and repeated scalar fields are rejected; output_formats may be repeated.

Field Default Meaning file Required One nonempty file, retaining its extension. tier Upstream default Optional flash/basic/standard/advanced, affecting PDFs/images only. ocr_mode auto auto/txt/ocr. page_range Whole document PDF ranges include 1-5, r1, and all; the upstream validates format-specific support. output_formats default default/docx/html/latex; repeat the field for a list, deduplicated in first-occurrence order. wait_timeout 3600 Integer seconds, 0–3600. request_id Generated 1–64 letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens; supply and save it before submission to recover after a disconnect.

Omitting tier lets the upstream choose Standard → Basic → Flash → Advanced for PDFs/images; Advanced is selected automatically only when it is the sole available tier. An explicitly unsupported PDF/image tier returns an error without substitution. Existing native documents always use Flash, even when a valid requested tier is not advertised upstream. Empty form strings and the literal string "null" are invalid tiers, not omissions.

output_formats is neither a JSON string nor a comma-separated value: use repeated form fields. include_model_output is removed and returns 400 when supplied.

docs.title: Upload and attachment responses
docs.text:
These are Bash/curl examples; in Windows PowerShell use curl.exe and adjust line continuations. The service calculates the size and hash from the actual uploaded file.

# response.body can be an attachment or JSON; check status and headers too.
curl --max-time 7200 -D response.headers -o response.body \
  http://127.0.0.1:8003/v1/file_parse \
  -F 'file=@report.pdf' \
  -F 'request_id=report-example' \
  -F 'tier=standard' \
  -F 'output_formats=default' -F 'output_formats=docx'
Endpoint HTTP Body POST, synchronous success 200 Raw attachment bytes, without a JSON/Base64 envelope. POST, wait expires or wait_timeout=0 202 Complete StatusResponse. GET /v1/file_parse/{request_id}, successful query 200 Complete StatusResponse, including known failure, cancellation, or unknown submission outcomes. GET /v1/file_parse/{request_id}/result, successful download 200 The same attachment as synchronous POST.

For an input named report.pdf:

output_formats Filename Content-Type / content default report.zip application/zip; Markdown, Middle JSON, Structured Content, images/. docx report.docx application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document; embedded images. html report.html text/html; charset=utf-8; embedded images. latex report.zip application/zip; document.tex, images/. Multiple formats report.zip A flat ZIP matching Tasks outputs.

Successful attachments include Content-Disposition, X-Request-ID, and X-Task-ID. A 202 includes Location (the status URL), Retry-After: 2, and X-Request-ID, plus X-Task-ID when confirmed. Status queries and error responses do not guarantee these headers; read recovery information from the JSON body.

docs.title: Status queries
docs.text:
All seven StatusResponse fields are always present. Nullable fields use null rather than the Tasks omission rule:

Field Type Meaning request_id string Wrapper request ID. task_id string or null Confirmed upstream task ID, or null before confirmation. status string Single-file state, listed below. status_url string Full query URL on the wrapper itself. result_url string or null Wrapper result endpoint when completed, otherwise null. output_formats string[] Normalized output format list. error object or null Latest stored error or upstream file error, otherwise null. State Meaning prepared Source and recovery record saved; not submitted yet. submitting Creating the upstream task without a confirmed task_id yet. waiting-file Upstream input preparation; an absent upload does not establish readiness. pending, running Queued, parsing, or exporting upstream. completed Upstream artifact ready; downloading may still fail due to expiry or transfer errors. failed, canceled Known failure or upstream cancellation. submission_unknown Creation may have succeeded, but no valid task ID was received; creation is not replayed automatically.

The wrapper processes one input and has no partial state. It exposes neither Tasks files/progress nor upstream signed URLs. Example 202 or GET status body:

{
  "request_id": "report-example",
  "task_id": "job_example",
  "status": "running",
  "status_url": "http://127.0.0.1:8003/v1/file_parse/report-example",
  "result_url": null,
  "output_formats": ["default", "docx"],
  "error": null
}

curl http://127.0.0.1:8003/v1/file_parse/report-example
curl --fail-with-body -D result.headers -o report.zip \
  http://127.0.0.1:8003/v1/file_parse/report-example/result

Downloads return 409 result_not_ready before completion, or potentially 409 task_not_created without a confirmed upstream task. Retry GET after an interrupted download. For an expired signature, the wrapper queries the original task and tries up to three times; unrecoverable expired results do not trigger reparsing.

docs.title: Waiting, idempotency, and recovery
docs.text:
wait_timeout starts after the upstream file is ready and covers queuing, parsing, and export. Receiving the source, upstream upload/download/validation, and result download use separate budgets, so this is not an overall HTTP request timeout. Normal polling is every two seconds; connection, metadata-request, and transfer-idle timeouts are 10, 30, and 600 seconds. Zero wait can be used to obtain a status-query entrypoint first.

The service takes responsibility only after receiving and persisting the entire source. Earlier disconnects do not create a task. Afterwards, client disconnects, wait timeouts, and wrapper shutdown do not automatically cancel upstream work.

  • The same request_id, file content, logical filename, and normalized parsing options reuse the original task; different input returns 409 request_id_conflict. wait_timeout is not part of request identity.
  • SQLite records are isolated by upstream address and authentication without storing the API key. Only one wrapper process may use a state directory. Restarts resume known tasks and still-valid pending uploads.
  • Creation task_id/file_id values are persisted before fetching details. A failed first query or a restart does not repeat creation. Unknown creation outcomes retain submission_unknown instead of being blindly retried.
  • Sources are removed after upstream readiness or terminal failure. Attachments are downloaded temporarily and removed after sending or interruption. Recovery records extend neither upstream upload links nor result retention; lost upstream tasks are not recreated.
  • The new protocol namespace uses tasks-v5-; old namespaces are neither loaded, migrated, nor automatically deleted. See 4.1 migration.

There is no separate wrapper cancellation endpoint. With a confirmed task_id and upstream authorization, POST /v1/tasks/{task_id}/cancel to the configured upstream API base, then query the wrapper to observe canceled. Do not use the wrapper base or confuse request_id with task_id. Without a saved ID or a received response, a caller may be unable to recover its request.

docs.title: Error responses
docs.text:
Errors directly generated by the wrapper contain code: string, message: string, and upstream_status: integer|null. Without a recovery record, only error is returned:

{
  "error": {
    "code": "unsupported_media_type",
    "message": "Expected multipart/form-data",
    "upstream_status": null
  }
}

With a record, the complete seven-field StatusResponse is returned with error replaced by the current operation's error. For example, an unfinished download returns HTTP 409 while status remains running. Stored errors in successful queries may also contain http_status or preserve upstream code/message and optional param. Historical recovery records may retain old type or other fields; tolerate these extensions without treating them as supported by the new Tasks protocol.

HTTP Common code Meaning 400 invalid_request, upload_interrupted Invalid parameters, multiple/empty files, or disconnect before acceptance. 404 request_not_found Record absent or collected. 408 upload_receive_timeout Idle timeout while receiving the request body. 409 request_id_conflict, result_not_ready, task_not_created, or cancellation codes Conflicting input, result not ready, no task yet, or upstream cancellation. 410 upload_expired Upstream upload window expired. 415 unsupported_media_type Not multipart/form-data. 500 storage_error Local storage failure. 502 submission_unknown, upstream_unreachable, upstream_protocol_error, invalid_result, or upstream codes Upstream request, transfer, parsing, or result-validation failure.

Upstream authentication failures return wrapper HTTP 502 with upstream_status=401. Explicit tier rejection also returns 502, preserving upstream 400/503; these are failed, not submission_unknown. Other creation-stage 5xx, 408, network failures, or malformed responses may leave acceptance unknown and become submission_unknown. A shared-schema 503 quality_tier_unavailable is a confirmed rejection. Neither case automatically replays creation; the same ID keeps the existing record.

docs.title: Python example client
docs.text:
The repository script requires httpx, prints the request ID before submission, and saves successful attachments atomically. On 202 it prints recovery information and exits with 124. Run from the repository root:

python scripts/http_file_parse_example.py report.pdf --output report.docx \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8003 --output-format docx --request-id report-docx

python scripts/http_file_parse_example.py report.pdf --wait-timeout 0 \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8003 --request-id report-background

docs.title: V1 HTTP API
docs.text:
In 4.1, Tasks is the single asynchronous parsing API. API Server, Router, the SDK and WebUI use a JSON files array, upload only missing files, poll task metadata and download each file's result. See the Tasks contract and Python SDK.

mineru-kit api-server --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --tier standard
MINERU_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 bash scripts/http_task_example.sh a.pdf b.pdf
OUTPUT_FORMATS=default,docx MINERU_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 bash scripts/http_api_example.sh a.pdf

docs.title: Create and upload
docs.text:
Send application/json to POST /v1/tasks. Each files entry requires file_name and, for uploads, bytes; sha256sum and page_range are optional. URL entries may omit bytes. Requests must not include client_file_id or file_id, even as null. The server generates a unique file_id for every entry and returns entries in input order. This ID remains stable through upload, query, cancellation and result download. Options are tier, ocr_mode, page_range and output_formats.

The response contains task_id and an upload object on each file that still needs uploading. files[].upload is omitted otherwise; its fields are url, headers and expires_at. Uploads always use PUT; upload_method is not returned. Follow each returned PUT URL and its headers; no completion request is needed. Each ready file enters pending independently. waiting-file covers upload, server-side download and validation; only a present upload object asks the client to send bytes. Input preparation consumes no parsing slot.

Loopback requests follow the same protocol. The SDK computes SHA-256 before submission; completed, unexpired cached inputs are not uploaded again. Concurrent first uploads may transfer duplicate bytes, but source storage is deduplicated. Default retention is 24 hours with collection every 5 minutes; active task and transfer references protect their bytes.

Upload links expire one hour after task creation. Queries do not renew them. Uploads accepted before the deadline may finish. After an uncertain upload, query first. pending/running/completed need no upload; waiting-file with no upload field requires polling only. Retry only when an upload target is available, within the transfer retry budget. A successful PUT is not repeated while waiting for confirmation.

docs.title: Status and results
docs.text:
Poll GET /v1/tasks/{task_id} using the configured API base, preserving its path prefix and URL-encoding the task ID. Bind the creation receipt to inputs in order, then match files by file_id. Parent states are waiting-file, pending, running, completed, partial, failed and canceled. Files use the same states except partial; upload_status has been removed. Each completed file has one files[].result_url; there is no top-level result_url or combined batch ZIP. Completed files can be downloaded while other files are still pending.

Outputs are default (Markdown, Middle JSON, Structured Content and images in a ZIP), docx, html, or latex (TEX and images in a ZIP). Multiple formats share one flat ZIP. DOCX and HTML embed images. ModelJson stays inside parsing and postprocessing; API, SDK, CLI and Gradio results do not include model output. The removed include_model_output option is rejected with HTTP 400, including false.

Task and file listing endpoints have been removed. POST /v1/tasks/{task_id}/cancel cancels unfinished files. Files metadata and output download remain available; task-record and artifact deletion endpoints are not provided. Before completion, files[].parse is omitted. Successful files report their actual tier, duration_ms and parser_version; there is no response-level tier. Responses no longer echo per-file sha256sum, page_range, private source IDs or duplicate name fields. Request parameters remain available.

Use returned result URLs directly. Local servers and Router return Files URLs; SaaS may return signed storage URLs. Attach the API key only to same-origin API requests and reevaluate credentials at every redirect. Query the task again when a result signature expires.

docs.title: Client and migration
docs.text:
Both shell examples delegate to the standard-library Python Tasks client. RESULT_DIR selects the per-file destination. OUTPUT_FORMATS defaults to default. SEND_HASH=0 disables the optional preflight hash. Resume with TASK_ID and the same input order.

Creation is not automatically retried. MAX_POLLS/POLL_INTERVAL bound polling; CONNECT_TIMEOUT/REQUEST_TIMEOUT bound individual requests. Exit codes are 0 (success), 2 (partial success), 1 (failure or cancellation) and 124 (poll budget exhausted). Completed downloads remain on disk.

Tasks and Files JSON use file_name; creation accepts files. Old manifest/filename fields and mixed old/new fields are rejected with 400. The standalone upload and Jobs APIs have been removed. Coordinate server, Router and SDK upgrades; see 4.1 migration. The separate file-parse wrapper provides recoverable synchronous single-file calls.

POST returns a creation receipt, GET returns task details, POST cancel returns every file’s final state and successful result links, and local PUT returns task_id/file_id/status. Tasks success responses omit null fields but preserve zero values and empty collections. POST cancel cancels unfinished files while preserving completed results.

docs.title: Single-file curl flow
docs.text:
Download the Bash example and prepare curl, jq, and an input file. Start a local API:

mineru-kit api-server --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --tier flash

In another terminal, run from the repository root:

MINERU_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
  bash docs/assets/examples/tasks-curl.sh report.html report.zip

The script creates a JSON task, PUTs the missing file, polls with GET, and downloads files[0].result_url. It uses the real file size, needs no complete request, and never retries task creation. It prints the receipt directory and task ID before polling; a polling timeout exits 124 while the task continues. Successful output is written to a new ZIP path; existing paths are rejected. Set MINERU_API_KEY when authentication is enabled.

This example only accepts upload and Files URLs from the same self-hosted API and does not follow redirects. Use the full Python client above for URL inputs, hashes, batch recovery, or signed object-storage links. PDF/image inference requires the selected tier's models; native HTML does not.

docs.title: Third-party integrations
docs.text:
The linked older tutorials are repository snapshots, not current platform instructions or evidence of local MinerU 4.1 compatibility. They are in Chinese.

Use Tasks for asynchronous local integrations, or the separate file-parse service for single-file multipart requests. Verify the plugin version and actual endpoints before upgrading; legacy /file_parse, Jobs, and upload-complete flows are incompatible.

Integration Tutorial scope BISHENG Historical tutorial; current compatibility unverified Cherry Studio Cloud/local configuration; local 4.1 requires separate validation Coze Historical tutorial; current compatibility unverified DataFlow Historical tutorial; current compatibility unverified Dify Cloud/local configuration; local 4.1 requires separate validation DingTalk Historical tutorial; current compatibility unverified FastGPT Historical tutorial; current compatibility unverified ModelWhale Historical tutorial; current compatibility unverified RagFlow Cloud/local configuration; local 4.1 requires separate validation Sider Historical tutorial; current compatibility unverified n8n Built-in ZIP workflow; instance validation still required

The n8n ZIP workflow downloads and extracts an existing result without a community parsing node.

docs.title: Model Downloads and Configuration
docs.text:
MinerU 4.0 configures small-model backends independently from VLM engines. Configuration defaults to $MINERU_HOME/config.yaml (MINERU_HOME defaults to ~/.mineru); MINERU_CONFIG selects another file.

model:
  source: auto
  base_dir: ~/.mineru/models
  small_backend: auto
  vlm:
    engine: auto

docs.title: Model sources
docs.text:
model.source accepts auto, huggingface, modelscope, and local. auto probes Hugging Face first and selects ModelScope when it is unavailable. Automatic selection from a default or config value may be written back to configuration. Environment variables override file settings:

export MINERU_MODEL_SOURCE=modelscope
mineru-kit parse document.pdf -o document.md --tier standard

Windows PowerShell:

$env:MINERU_MODEL_SOURCE = "modelscope"

The small-model bundles MinerU-4_models_torch and MinerU-4_models_onnx are registered for both Hugging Face and ModelScope. Original VLM weights and llama.cpp GGUF/mmproj use different repositories selected by the engine. Basic needs the selected small-model bundle; Standard also needs VLM models and serves Advanced requests.

docs.title: Download, verify, and run offline
docs.text:
Download and verify a Standard deployment using the current configuration:

mineru-kit models download --tier standard --source huggingface
mineru-kit models verify --tier standard
mineru-kit models show

An explicit CPU small-model and llama.cpp combination:

mineru-kit models download --tier standard --small-backend onnx --vlm-engine llama-cpp --source huggingface
mineru-kit models verify --tier standard --small-backend onnx --vlm-engine llama-cpp

A NVIDIA / vLLM deployment can download its models on a build machine without a GPU. Specify the target backends instead of relying on that machine's automatic selection:

mineru-kit models download --tier standard --small-backend torch --vlm-engine vllm --source huggingface
mineru-kit models verify --tier standard --small-backend torch --vlm-engine vllm

These command options apply only to the current operation and do not change persistent configuration. Use the same combination for inference, for example:

export MINERU_MODEL_SMALL_BACKEND=torch
export MINERU_MODEL_VLM_ENGINE=vllm
export MINERU_MODEL_SOURCE=local
mineru-kit parse document.pdf -o document.md --tier standard

Use basic as the download tier when no VLM is needed. Advanced has no separate deployment download tier. Set model.base_dir before downloading to change the model root. Completion markers and required files determine readiness. Repeated downloads reuse provider caches; do not create completion markers manually.

local uses ready local models and fails on missing assets without downloading. An explicit models download is a download operation: even with local configured, it temporarily resolves a remote source automatically.

Explicit mlx is also supported for local VLM inference. It is never selected by auto mode and is not a MinerU extra. See extension modules for its separate installation.

docs.title: Remote VLM service
docs.text:
An existing model.vlm.server_url takes priority and removes the local VLM weight requirement. This is a model inference endpoint, not the MinerU V1 document parsing API. Small-model requirements still depend on the tier. The full field set:

Field Default Purpose model.vlm.engine auto Local engine selection: auto/llama-cpp/vllm/lmdeploy/mlx; not used while a remote server_url is set model.vlm.server_url (unset) Remote VLM inference endpoint. Must be HTTP(S) without credentials, query, or fragment; a trailing /v1 is stripped and the URL is kept ending with / (reverse-proxy path prefixes are preserved) model.vlm.api_key (unset) Bearer key for the remote VLM service; environment variable MINERU_MODEL_VLM_API_KEY model.vlm.model (unset) Model name requested from the remote service; environment variable MINERU_MODEL_VLM_MODEL model.vlm.http_timeout 600 Per-request timeout in seconds model.vlm.max_concurrency 100 Maximum concurrent VLM requests

Legacy MINERU_VL_API_KEY / MINERU_VL_MODEL_NAME are rejected when they conflict with these fields; see the migration guide.

model.stack, MINERU_MODEL_STACK, and --stack have been removed. Restart relevant services after configuration changes.

docs.title: Three remote connections at a glance
docs.text:
MinerU talks to three different kinds of remote services. They are not interchangeable — do not reuse one service's address, key, or model name for another:

Connection Purpose Where it is configured V1 document parsing service Upload documents, submit parse jobs, download results (self-hosted mineru-kit api-server, router, or the official cloud service) Per client: MINERU_API_URL / MINERU_API_KEY, or SDK MinerUApiParser(api_url=..., api_key=...). The document library's default remote target is a library runtime setting, not part of config.yaml Remote VLM inference service Model inference for local parse pipelines (Standard/Advanced), OpenAI-compatible model.vlm.server_url / api_key / model in config.yaml LLM-aided post-processing Title leveling and cross-page table cell continuation llm_aided.api_key / base_url / model in config.yaml; both features are disabled by default

docs.title: Download troubleshooting
docs.text: Hugging Face uses hf_xet by default. If your network cannot reach Xet CAS, set HF_HUB_DISABLE_XET=1 before downloading to use regular HTTP, or switch to ModelScope. For offline deployment, download and verify before selecting local. See extension modules for installation combinations.

docs.title: PDF memory regression checks
docs.text: Window lifetime improvements are always active. MINERU_MALLOC_TRIM independently enables optional CPU heap trimming and is off by default. Measure real workloads on Linux/glibc before claiming an RSS improvement or an OOM fix; macOS checks cannot establish either.

docs.title: Compare three configurations
docs.text:
Use the same host, Python environment, DocVortex version, models, settings, and concurrency. Create a separate worktree at the pre-change commit without switching or overwriting your development checkout.

Activate the project Python environment and install the diagnostic-only dependency with uv pip install psutil. Run the updated script from your development checkout. --repo selects the child process's MinerU source; third-party dependencies still come from the current Python environment.

python scripts/benchmark_pdf_memory.py --repo /tmp/mineru-memory-baseline --pdf demo/pdfs/demo1.pdf demo/pdfs/demo2.pdf --tier basic --mode ocr --window-size 2 --trim 0 --output /tmp/mineru-memory-before
python scripts/benchmark_pdf_memory.py --pdf demo/pdfs/demo1.pdf demo/pdfs/demo2.pdf --tier basic --mode ocr --window-size 2 --trim 0 --output /tmp/mineru-memory-after-off
python scripts/benchmark_pdf_memory.py --pdf demo/pdfs/demo1.pdf demo/pdfs/demo2.pdf --tier basic --mode ocr --window-size 2 --trim 1 --output /tmp/mineru-memory-after-on

Each group starts a fresh parser process, warms up for three rounds, and measures twenty rounds. One document is processed per round, cycling through multiple inputs in order and releasing the preceding result. Output directories must not already exist.

  • For repeated-document checks, pass one PDF. For alternating documents, pass two or more.
  • For multiple windows, use a document longer than --window-size. This affects only the experiment, not product defaults.
  • Exercise basic/standard/advanced with txt/ocr, plus flash --mode ocr, using the required models and VLM configuration.
  • Without neural models, flash --mode txt can validate the harness, document cleanup, and selective rendering. It cannot validate inference-window allocation lifetimes or inference performance.

docs.title: Outputs and interpretation
docs.text:
• rounds.jsonl: input, page count, parse duration, and timestamps per round, marking warmup rounds.
  • samples.jsonl: externally sampled RSS/USS for the parser and all child PIDs every 0.2 seconds. Unavailable USS is null; change frequency with --interval.
  • parse.log: production logs with window ranges and render-worker PIDs for correlation.
  • summary.json: measured-round median parse time, per-PID peaks, and simultaneous process-total peaks. Summed RSS can double-count shared pages, and sampling can miss brief peaks.

Inspect the parent and workers separately. Compare post-warmup trends, plateaus, peaks, and timing. Investigate a median slowdown above 5% with trimming disabled after excluding concurrent workloads, cold model startup, and sampling noise. Report enabled-trim overhead separately and repeat the complete experiment before drawing conclusions.

Trimming cannot release live results, model caches, other allocators' pools, another process's memory, or objects still referenced by exception tracebacks. DocVortex worker reclamation is outside this change.

docs.title: Output parity
docs.text:
In separate output directories, add --warmup 0 --rounds 2 --fingerprints to each configuration. Compare middle_sha256 for matching inputs; hashes include full asset fields. Fingerprinting performs extra serialization, so do not use these runs for memory or performance conclusions.

If Linux, models, or USS access are unavailable, record that limitation explicitly and keep trimming disabled by default.

docs.title: Quick Model Source Configuration
docs.text:
MinerU defaults to auto: probe Hugging Face first and choose ModelScope when it is unavailable. If users cannot access huggingface due to network restrictions, they can conveniently switch the model source to modelscope through environment variables: 

export MINERU_MODEL_SOURCE=modelscope
For more information about model source configuration and custom local model paths, please refer to the Model Source Documentation in the documentation.

docs.title: Quick Usage via Command Line
docs.text:
MinerU has built-in command line tools that allow users to quickly use MinerU for document parsing through the command line: 

mineru parse <input_path> -o <output_path>

Tip

  • <input_path>: One local PDF / OFD / EPUB / static HTML / MHTML (.mhtml or .mht) / image / CSV / RTF / DOC/DOCX / PPT/PPTX / XLS/XLSX / ODT/ODS/ODP file
  • <output_path>: Optional output file; without it, Markdown is written to stdout
  • PDF parsing defaults to the first 10 pages; use --pages all for the full PDF. Non-PDF inputs, including MHTML, are parsed as whole documents and do not accept --pages.

For more information about output files, please refer to Output File Documentation.

Note

Runtime acceleration is selected separately for the two model components, based on installed dependencies and detected devices:

  • Small models use the Torch backend only when torch, torchvision, transformers, accelerate, and safetensors are all installed and a non-CPU device (CUDA/MPS/...) is detected; otherwise they use ONNX. In 4.1, ONNX selects compatible DirectML/WebGPU acceleration or CPU on Windows/Linux; see Tiers and runtimes. Installing Torch alone is not enough.
  • The local VLM engine is chosen independently: macOS always uses llama.cpp; on an accelerator device Linux prefers vLLM, then an installed LMDeploy, and Windows uses LMDeploy; otherwise llama.cpp.
  • XPU is excluded from automatic LMDeploy selection: Linux uses an installed XPU-compatible vLLM, otherwise llama.cpp; Windows uses llama.cpp.
  • Windows users who need CUDA acceleration should first visit the PyTorch website and install accelerator-enabled torch and torchvision matching their CUDA version, then install the mineru[full] extras.

After installation, confirm the runtimes actually in effect in your environment:

mineru-kit models show

The output reports Effective small backend and Effective VLM engine together with the config source of each value. models show displays effective backends, engines, and model readiness — missing model files are reported but do not fail the command; use mineru-kit models verify when a non-zero exit code should signal incomplete model files. Neither command runs inference. A full validation progresses in order: dependencies installed → selection as expected → models verify passes → a small sample document actually parses successfully. See Tiers and Runtimes for the full selection table.

If you need to adjust parsing options through custom parameters, you can also check the more detailed Command Line Tools Usage Instructions in the documentation.

docs.title: Library, search, and continuation
docs.text:
mineru keeps file identity, parsing caches, and indexes in a local document library. Responses include locators; replace the example document ID below with an actual returned ID:

mineru parse document.pdf --json
mineru search "keyword" --json
mineru read "doc:ab12cd3/tier:standard/page:11" --json

When an output reaches its budget, follow next_request or the returned continuation command. read consumes existing results without automatically starting higher-quality parsing. Use mineru-kit parse for stateless batches and complete exports. Native Office, HTML/MHTML, CSV/TSV, EPUB, and OFD normalize to local Flash.

docs.title: Advanced Usage via API, WebUI, and Services
docs.text:
• Start the self-hosted V1 API: 

    mineru-kit api-server --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --tier standard

    Tip

    Access http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs for the OpenAPI documentation. The supported service surface is /v1/*, including health, capability discovery, Tasks creation and operations by ID, per-file uploads, result downloads, and usage. Task and file lists are not exposed.

    Native document parsing example: Python SDK; plain HTTP: V1 HTTP API

  • Start Gradio WebUI visual frontend: 

    mineru-kit webui --server-name 0.0.0.0 --server-port 7860

    Tip

    • Access http://127.0.0.1:7860 in your browser to use the Gradio WebUI.
    • Without --api-url, Gradio manages a loopback mineru-kit api-server; with --api-url, it connects only to that existing V1 service.
    • Use --api-server-preload-models to preload models for the managed local server.
    • mineru-webui remains available as a command-name alias with the same modern options.

  • Use mineru-router for multi-service / multi-GPU orchestration: 

    mineru-router --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8002 --local-gpus auto --worker-tier standard

    Tip

    • mineru-router and mineru-kit router expose the complete /v1/* API.
    • Repeat --upstream-url to aggregate multiple existing V1 api-server services, or use --local-gpus to launch mineru-kit api-server workers automatically.
    • Use --preload-models for router-managed workers; remote upstreams keep their own startup configuration.
    • Unknown model-engine arguments are not forwarded by Router.
    • It is intended for advanced multi-service, multi-GPU, and unified-entry deployments.

  • Start an OpenAI-compatible VLM server: 

    mineru-kit vlm-server --engine auto --port 30000

Note

Model-engine parameters apply only to commands that explicitly declare them. mineru-router accepts documented Router/worker options and does not forward unknown arguments. We have compiled some commonly used parameters and usage methods for vllm/lmdeploy, which can be found in the documentation Advanced Command Line Parameters.

docs.title: Configuring LLM-aided post-processing with config.yaml
docs.text:
LLM-aided title leveling and cross-page table cell continuation read $MINERU_HOME/config.yaml and support OpenAI-compatible model services:

llm_aided:
  api_key: ${MINERU_LLM_API_KEY:-}
  base_url: https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1
  model: qwen3.5-plus
  enable_thinking: false
  max_concurrency: 16
  features:
    title_leveling: false
    cross_page_table_cell_merge: false
  • title_leveling groups paragraph titles into levels 2 through 6 by document-title boundaries and runs only when MiddleJson.is_full_document is true. Page-selected input is persisted as false and skips title leveling.
  • cross_page_table_cell_merge asks the LLM whether each pair of boundary-row cells continues after the existing rules identify a cross-page table.
  • Table cell merge does not require whole-document input. Both features are disabled by default and share one asynchronous client, one connection configuration, and the max_concurrency request limit, which defaults to 16.
  • max_concurrency must be an integer of at least 1 and can be overridden with MINERU_LLM_AIDED_MAX_CONCURRENCY.
  • Enabling either feature requires non-empty api_key, base_url, and model values.
  • enable_thinking is optional. When omitted, the extension parameter is not sent to the model service.
  • The legacy llm-aided-config section in mineru.json is no longer read.

docs.title: Extending MinerU Functionality with Configuration Files
docs.text:
MinerU works out of the box and reads current settings from $MINERU_HOME/config.yaml; set MINERU_CONFIG to use another file. Legacy mineru.json CLI settings are no longer supported.

Model storage and source settings use the model section:

model:
  base_dir: ~/.mineru/models
  source: auto
  small_backend: auto
  vlm:
    engine: auto

See Model Source Documentation for model download and local-source details.

docs.title: PDF page selection
docs.text: Use --pages "1-5,8,r3-r1": page numbers start at 1, ranges include both endpoints, and r1 means the last page. Use all for every page. Results are sorted and deduplicated; partially out-of-bounds ranges select their valid intersection. Reversed or empty selections fail with page_range_invalid. Without --pages, mineru parse starts with the first 10 pages; mineru-kit parse, Python and Gradio select all pages. New requests use the current syntax. Historical positive result ranges using ASCII ~ remain readable without rebuilding Doclib caches; result responses and new cache entries use -. Fullwidth ～ and negative page-number notation are not supported. See page-range syntax and historical result compatibility.

docs.title: Local Python SDK
docs.text:
mineru.parser exports stateless parse, parse_async, MinerUParser, and a shared ParseResult; it does not create a document library. PDF page ranges default to all pages; page_range="1-3" uses one-based page numbers.

from pathlib import Path
from mineru.parser import parse, ParseResult

result = parse("document.pdf", tier="flash", ocr_mode="txt", page_range="1-3")
Path("document.md").write_text(result.markdown(), encoding="utf-8")
Path("document.json").write_text(result.to_json(), encoding="utf-8")
restored = ParseResult.from_json(result.to_json())
assert restored.to_dict() == result.to_dict()

For native documents, use parse("report.docx", tier="flash") without a PDF page range. For higher-quality PDF/image parsing, select tier="standard" or tier="advanced" and prepare the relevant runtime and models.

The asynchronous entrypoint accepts the same parsing options:

import asyncio
from mineru.parser import parse_async

result = asyncio.run(parse_async("report.docx", tier="flash"))
print(result.markdown())

Inside an existing event loop, use await parse_async(...). An async interface does not imply identical execution mechanisms across engines.

docs.title: Connect to a self-hosted V1 API
docs.text:
Start the service in its inference environment:

mineru-kit api-server --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --tier standard

The Python client handles discovery, file submission, task polling, and result downloads:

from mineru.parser import MinerUApiParser

parser = MinerUApiParser(
    api_url="http://127.0.0.1:8000",
    tier="standard",
    include_images=True,
)
result = parser.parse("document.pdf", page_range="1-3")
print(result.markdown())

api_url is the service root before /v1. Use MINERU_API_KEY for a configured key instead of embedding credentials in source. Connecting to another machine may upload files to that service. The WebUI can use the same address:

mineru-kit webui --api-url http://127.0.0.1:8000

docs.title: Batching and instance reuse
docs.text:
Reuse one MinerUApiParser instance for batch work instead of constructing a parser per file; each call opens and closes its own HTTP session, so there is nothing to release explicitly. HTTP failures are expressed as task statuses and per-file error entries; the Python SDK converts failed/canceled terminal tasks (and network/HTTP errors) into exceptions, so batch code should catch per file, record a summary, and exit with an explicit policy:

import sys
from pathlib import Path
from mineru.parser import MinerUApiParser

pdfs = sorted(Path("./documents").glob("*.pdf"))
if not pdfs:
    sys.exit("no input files under ./documents")

output_dir = Path("out")
output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

parser = MinerUApiParser(api_url="http://127.0.0.1:8000", tier="standard", include_images=True)
failures: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
for pdf in pdfs:
    try:
        result = parser.parse(str(pdf))
        (output_dir / f"{pdf.stem}.md").write_text(result.markdown(), encoding="utf-8")
    except Exception as exc:  # terminal job failures and transport errors both raise
        failures.append((pdf.name, str(exc)))
        print(f"failed: {pdf.name}: {exc}")

if failures:
    sys.exit(f"{len(failures)} of {len(pdfs)} files failed")

When throughput matters, check the service logs and GET /v1/usage. See Tiers and Runtimes for choosing tier and the V1 HTTP API walkthrough for the underlying request cycle.

docs.title: HTTP API without the SDK
docs.text:
The same create → upload → poll → download cycle can be driven with plain HTTP calls. The V1 HTTP API walkthrough provides a single-file curl flow and a resumable script client for PUT uploads, terminal states, and downloads. No upload-complete request is needed.

The 4.1 main API uses /v1/tasks and does not provide legacy /file_parse or /tasks routes. The separate wrapper serves /v1/file_parse. See migration for older clients and output formats for rendering and saving Python results.

docs.title: Tasks API
docs.text: This page describes the 4.1.0 contract. /v1/tasks is the shared asynchronous parsing API for API Server, Router, and compatible SaaS: submit a JSON manifest, upload missing files, poll, and download results per file. Existing clients should read the 4.1 migration guide. For synchronous single-file requests, see the file-parse API.

docs.title: Startup and authentication
docs.text:
mineru-kit api-server --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --tier auto

The service exposes deployment-specific definitions at /docs and /openapi.json. When an API key is configured, send Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY> on API requests. Local services without a key do not require that header. The API base may include a reverse-proxy path prefix.

Method and path Success response Purpose POST /v1/tasks 202, CreateTaskResponse Submit a JSON manifest. PUT files[].upload.url Local/Router: 200, UploadFileResponse Upload one file's raw bytes; accept successful 2xx responses from object storage. GET /v1/tasks/{task_id} 200, TaskDetailResponse Read a complete status snapshot. POST /v1/tasks/{task_id}/cancel 200, CancelTaskResponse Cancel unfinished files; no request body required.

Local upload paths are /v1/tasks/{task_id}/uploads/{file_id}; clients should use the returned full URL. There are no task/file lists, public DELETE operations, or batch-result endpoint. The main API Server and Router do not expose /v1/file_parse.

docs.title: Creation request
docs.text:
POST /v1/tasks accepts only application/json. Put all business parameters in the JSON body. Query parameters, unknown fields, and invalid values return 400; other content types return 415.

Field Type Default or requirement files object[] Required, 1–100 entries; not a JSON-encoded string. tier string or null Optional; flash/basic/standard/advanced, as described below. ocr_mode string auto; accepts auto/txt/ocr. page_range string Empty means the whole document; PDF ranges include 1-5, r1, and all. output_formats string[] ["default"]; nonempty, values from default/docx/html/latex, deduplicated in first-occurrence order.

Each files[] entry:

Field Type Requirement file_name string Required logical filename, 1–1024 characters, retaining its extension. Duplicate names are allowed. bytes integer or null Required positive integer for uploads. Optional for URLs; when supplied, must match the actual size. url string or null HTTP(S) download URL; omitted or null means a client upload. sha256sum string or null Optional 64-character lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 for validation and, for uploads, cache preflight. page_range string or null Optional per-file PDF range overriding the global range. Non-PDF native documents still parse as a whole.

Requests must omit file_id/client_file_id, including null values. The server allocates public file_id values in input order; duplicate names or content still receive different IDs. Use IDs to correlate uploads, queries, cancellation, and downloads. Local/Router result Files IDs match these IDs; Files lookup returns 404 before the result exists. Source-cache IDs remain private.

docs.title: Tier selection
docs.text:
• For PDFs/images, an omitted or null tier selects the first supported value in standard → basic → flash → advanced order. Advanced is selected automatically only when it is the sole available tier.
  • An explicitly unsupported PDF/image tier rejects the entire creation request with 400 invalid_request, error.param="tier". No work is accepted and no tier substitution occurs.
  • Every normally available compatible service supports existing native document formats. Office, HTML, and other native documents always use Flash, regardless of /v1/tiers or a valid requested tier. Empty strings and unknown enum values are still invalid.
  • Mixed batches select tiers per file. On a Standard-capable service, a PDF + DOCX request without a tier uses Standard and Flash respectively. Selection is fixed at admission, not repeated during queuing or forwarding. Successful files report the actual value in parse.tier.

docs.title: Example request and creation receipt
docs.text:
Sizes, IDs, URLs, and timestamps below are illustrative; use the actual byte count for a real upload.

{
  "files": [{"file_name": "report.pdf", "bytes": 12345}],
  "tier": "standard",
  "ocr_mode": "auto",
  "output_formats": ["default", "docx"]
}

202 creation receipt:

{
  "task_id": "job_example",
  "status": "waiting-file",
  "files": [{
    "file_id": "file-example",
    "file_name": "report.pdf",
    "status": "waiting-file",
    "upload": {
      "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/tasks/job_example/uploads/file-example",
      "headers": {},
      "expires_at": 1800003600
    }
  }]
}

202 means accepted. Creation receipts omit input sizes, parsing statistics, and result URLs; use GET for details even if a file has already completed.

URL inputs use the same creation endpoint, for example:

{
  "files": [{"file_name": "report.pdf", "url": "https://example.com/report.pdf"}],
  "output_formats": ["html"]
}

The server downloads URL inputs without a client PUT; replace the example with a real download URL allowed by the deployment.

docs.title: Response fields
docs.text:
Success responses are direct objects without a data/task envelope. Below, ? marks an optional field and is not part of its name.

Response Top-level fields files[] fields CreateTaskResponse task_id, status, files file_id, file_name, status, upload? TaskDetailResponse task_id, status, created_at, started_at?, finished_at?, output_formats, progress, files, error? file_id, file_name, status, bytes?, url?, upload?, parse?, result_url?, error? CancelTaskResponse task_id, status (always canceled), finished_at, files file_id, file_name, status, parse?, result_url?, error? UploadFileResponse task_id, file_id, status (the uploaded file's state) None

task_id/file_id/file_name/status are strings, files is an array, bytes is an integer, url/result_url are strings, and output_formats is a string array. Time fields are ISO-8601 UTC strings.

Nested object Fields and meaning upload url: string, headers: object (string pairs, possibly empty), expires_at: integer (Unix seconds). Present only when an upload is currently needed. parse tier: string, duration_ms?: integer, parser_version?: string. Successful files only; version identifies the executing worker. Duration includes source reading/downloading, validation, parsing, and export, excluding waits for upload, preparation slots, or parsing queues. progress Required integers completed/failed/total. Canceled files count as neither completed nor failed; total is the number of inputs. error Required nonempty code: string, message: string, and param?: string. May appear at the GET top level, in GET files, or in failed files of cancellation receipts; no type field.

Tasks success responses recursively omit nulls, preserving 0/false/[]/{}. Each response is a complete snapshot: an absent field has no current value, so do not retain stale upload links. Clients should tolerate future extra fields. Public HTTP errors also omit absent param values; Files and file-parse use separate null rules.

Example completed GET response (200):

{
  "task_id": "job_example",
  "status": "completed",
  "created_at": "2026-10-28T00:00:00Z",
  "started_at": "2026-10-28T00:00:02Z",
  "finished_at": "2026-10-28T00:00:10Z",
  "output_formats": ["default", "docx"],
  "progress": {"completed": 1, "failed": 0, "total": 1},
  "files": [{
    "file_id": "file-example",
    "file_name": "report.pdf",
    "status": "completed",
    "bytes": 12345,
    "parse": {"tier": "standard", "duration_ms": 8000, "parser_version": "4.1.0"},
    "result_url": "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/files/file-example/content"
  }]
}

Example local PUT receipt: {"task_id":"job_example","file_id":"file-example","status":"pending"}. Successful object-storage PUT responses need not contain this JSON; query Tasks afterwards to confirm readiness.

docs.title: Uploads, URLs, and caching
docs.text:
PUT raw bytes using the returned upload.url/headers; no completion call is required. Upload only when a file is waiting-file and has an upload object. Otherwise poll. Each validated file queues independently without waiting for other files; waiting uploads do not reserve parsing capacity.

  • Valid hash-based cache hits skip uploads. Only source bytes are reused; each task parses with its own parameters. Concurrent first uploads may transfer duplicate bytes, but source storage is deduplicated.
  • URL inputs are downloaded by the server without an upload action, HEAD requirement, or Content-Length requirement. file_name determines the format; actual bytes are populated after download and supplied sizes/hashes are checked. URLs are downloaded each time, without hash-based download skipping.
  • Local URL sources default to HTTPS only. HTTP requires --allow-http-source; defaults are a 60-second download timeout and a 200 MiB size limit. Direct client uploads have no fixed size or PDF page limit, though deployments may impose gateway limits.
  • Upload links expire 3600 seconds after creation and are not renewed by polling. Uploads admitted before the deadline may finish; files not yet admitted become failed/upload_expired. Processing of successfully uploaded files is not limited by this deadline.
  • Do not repeat successful PUTs. Query after a lost response: skip upload for pending/running/completed, poll waiting-file without an upload object, and retry within bounds only after failure when a valid upload action remains. Expired uploads need a new task. Chunk-level resumable uploads are not supported.

Local source caches default to 24-hour retention with collection every five minutes; active tasks and transfers protect source bytes. API/Router task records and indexes are in memory and are not guaranteed to survive restarts.

docs.title: Dynamic Router upstreams and cascading
docs.text:
A running Router can register, inspect, and safely deregister remote upstreams. An upstream can be a V1 API Server or another Router. Management affects only the receiving Router; it does not deregister downstream workers or stop remote processes. Locally managed workers are excluded.

Set an independent management key to enable the endpoints. Without a key, these paths return 404. --admin-api-key overrides MINERU_ROUTER_ADMIN_API_KEY and also works with --reload. This key is separate from parsing credentials and is never forwarded downstream; parsing authentication is unchanged.

# An empty pool can start: health returns 503 until a healthy upstream is added,
# while the management endpoints remain available.
export MINERU_ROUTER_ADMIN_API_KEY='replace-with-a-management-secret'
mineru-kit router --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8002 --local-gpus none

# Set the same key in another terminal before running these requests.
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8002/v1/router/workers \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MINERU_ROUTER_ADMIN_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"url":"http://worker-a:8000"}'
curl http://127.0.0.1:8002/v1/router/workers \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MINERU_ROUTER_ADMIN_API_KEY"
# Use the worker_id returned by registration or listing.
curl -i -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:8002/v1/router/workers/remote-1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MINERU_ROUTER_ADMIN_API_KEY"
Endpoint Response and behavior GET /v1/router/workers 200, with {"object":"list","data":[...]} containing both startup-configured and dynamically registered remote nodes. POST /v1/router/workers Accepts only url. Returns 201 for a new URL or 200 for an existing normalized URL. Re-registration preserves its ID and references and resumes a draining node. DELETE /v1/router/workers/{worker_id} Returns 204 after removal if no references remain, or 202 with a draining snapshot otherwise. Unknown and locally managed nodes return 404 worker_not_found.

Each node snapshot contains worker_id, url, state (active/draining), healthy, tiers, active_jobs, and retained_routes. URLs must be HTTP/HTTPS base URLs; path prefixes are supported, while embedded credentials, query strings, and fragments are rejected. Invalid input returns 400 invalid_request; missing or incorrect management credentials return 401 invalid_api_key. Errors use error.code/message and optional param.

Registration performs an initial health and capability probe. An unreachable node or one returning invalid tier data remains registered with healthy=false and is retried by the existing periodic checks. Invalid capabilities do not replace the last valid snapshot or break management listing. Only healthy, active nodes participate in new scheduling and health/models/tiers aggregation. A successful health check does not undo draining.

Deregistration stops new reservations immediately. Existing reservations, upload handoffs, queries, cancellation, result leases, and downloads continue. Removal waits for execution reservations, requests/streams, execution and file routes, and leases to be released; active_jobs=0 alone does not mean the remote service can stop. Results default to 24-hour retention, so a node may remain draining during that period. The five-minute collection loop removes eligible nodes; repeating DELETE also checks eligibility. With --retention-seconds 0, permanent result references can prevent removal indefinitely. There is no force-delete operation.

Files that have not yet been dispatched use the remaining eligible nodes. If none qualify, they fail with the existing quality_tier_unavailable error; no implicit tier downgrade or new waiting queue is introduced. Removing the last node is allowed. Absence from this Router's list only means this Router has released its references; the downstream service may still serve other callers.

For a two-level deployment, configure the outer Router with inner Router URLs:

mineru-kit router --local-gpus none \
  --upstream-url http://router-a:8002 \
  --upstream-url http://router-b:8002

The same POST endpoint can add Router C at runtime. Use independent worker pools below each inner Router and an acyclic topology. Global load accounting and cross-Router task takeover are not provided.

Dynamic membership lasts only for the current process. Registration and deregistration do not modify startup configuration. Restarting restores the --upstream-url list; dynamic nodes must be registered again, and worker IDs are not stable across restarts. The outer Router remains a single point of failure, and existing tasks are not guaranteed to recover after any Router restarts.

docs.title: States and cancellation
docs.text:
File state Meaning waiting-file Waiting for/receiving uploads, URL downloads, validation, or object-storage confirmation. pending Input ready, waiting for parsing resources. running Parsing, exporting, or saving results. completed All requested formats succeeded; the result is downloadable. failed Input, parsing, or export failed; inspect error. canceled An unfinished file was canceled.

Parent aggregation prioritizes running, then pending, then waiting-file. All successful files yield completed; terminal success/failure mixtures yield partial; no successes yield failed. Cancellation sets the parent to canceled. A parent may move from running back to waiting-file while completed files remain downloadable.

Cancellation preserves completed/failed files and marks the others canceled. Receipt file states are therefore limited to completed/failed/canceled. Non-interruptible computation or cleanup may still finish internally, but late results cannot overwrite published cancellation states. Canceling an already terminal task returns 409 task_already_terminal.

Example 200 receipt for canceling a single-file task that is still processing:

{
  "task_id": "job_example",
  "status": "canceled",
  "finished_at": "2026-10-28T00:00:05Z",
  "files": [{"file_id": "file-example", "file_name": "report.pdf", "status": "canceled"}]
}

docs.title: Outputs and downloads
docs.text:
output_formats Result per input ["default"] ZIP with markdown.md, middle_json.json, structured_content.json, and images/. ["docx"] A DOCX with embedded images. ["html"] An HTML file with embedded images; formula scripts retain renderer behavior. ["latex"] ZIP with document.tex and images/. Multiple formats One flat ZIP, without nested ZIPs; DOCX/HTML names are document.docx/document.html.

Each input is parsed once. One files[].result_url is published after all requested formats succeed. If any format fails, that file becomes failed/result_packaging_failed without partial artifacts; other files continue. There is no combined batch ZIP or top-level result_url. Completed files can be downloaded before the parent finishes.

ModelJson is internal. include_model_output is removed and returns 400 even when false; results do not contain model_output.json.

Local services and Router return Files URLs; SaaS may return signed object-storage URLs. Use returned result URLs without constructing storage paths. Attach the API key only to same-origin API requests, reevaluating every redirect; never forward it to object storage. During result retention, query again to renew an expired download signature. Polling and downloads do not render again, and unfinished files do not cause completed results to be collected early.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Request-level errors use a non-2xx status and {"error": ...}, for example:

{
  "error": {
    "code": "task_already_terminal",
    "message": "Task is canceled"
  }
}
HTTP Common code Scenario 400 invalid_request, page_range_invalid Invalid fields, tiers, ranges, or old parameters. 400 upload_size_mismatch, file_hash_mismatch, upload_interrupted Upload validation or transfer failure. 401 invalid_api_key Invalid credentials on an authenticated service. 404 task_not_found, upload_not_found Task unavailable/collected, or no such upload file ID. 409 task_already_terminal, file_already_terminal Canceling a terminal task or uploading to a file no longer accepting bytes. 410 upload_expired Upload window expired. 415 invalid_request Creation request is not JSON. 503 quality_tier_unavailable, server_shutting_down, or model preload codes The service cannot accept the request.

Asynchronous download, parsing, and export failures usually appear in files[].error inside a 200 query snapshot; HTTP 200 does not mean parsing succeeded. Public errors contain required nonempty code, message, and optional param; type is neither emitted nor accepted. Absent param values are omitted, although receivers also accept null. Branch on HTTP status and code rather than parsing message text. Inspect every file's state: an absent top-level error does not establish that all files succeeded.

docs.title: Runnable client examples
docs.text:
Run these Bash examples from the repository root. The standard-library Python client calculates real sizes and hashes, uploads files, and downloads per-file results:

MINERU_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
  bash scripts/http_task_example.sh report.pdf notes.docx

OUTPUT_FORMATS=default,docx RESULT_DIR=results \
MINERU_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
  bash scripts/http_task_example.sh report.pdf

# Resume with the original file list and order, without creating again.
TASK_ID=job_example MINERU_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
  bash scripts/http_task_example.sh report.pdf

Set MINERU_API_KEY for authentication, MINERU_TIER/OCR_MODE/PAGE_RANGE for parsing options, and SEND_HASH=0 to disable hash preflight. MAX_POLLS/POLL_INTERVAL default to 300/1 and bound polling; CONNECT_TIMEOUT/REQUEST_TIMEOUT bound individual transfers. Creation is not automatically retried. Exit codes: 0 all successful, 2 partial success, 1 failure/cancellation, 124 polling exhausted. Completed downloads remain on disk.

For direct HTTP calls, append /v1/tasks/{URL-encoded task_id} to the configured API base for queries, and append /cancel to that route for POST cancellation. Save creation IDs for recovery; Tasks does not return a status_url.

docs.title: Tiers and Runtimes
docs.text:
Tiers express parsing quality and cost. Small-model backends and VLM engines are configured independently; they are not tier names.

This page includes 4.1 device-selection and service-tier behavior. Existing deployments should follow the 4.1 migration guide.

Tier Purpose Local execution flash Fast previews, indexing, native documents Native PDF text / document parsing; Flash OCR for scans and images basic OCR, formulas, and tables ONNX or Torch small models; no local VLM required standard Complex layouts and high-quality parsing Small models + VLM advanced More demanding quality requirements Standard models and runtime, with more inference computation

PDF and images support all four tiers. Office, OpenDocument, RTF, EPUB, OFD, HTML/MHTML, and CSV/TSV use local Flash and whole-document parsing. Pass tier="flash" explicitly for these formats in the local Python SDK. MHTML web archives (.mhtml, .mht) are parsed as whole documents. Plain text is not parsed, but can be indexed and read by the document library.

For a saved web page archive:

mineru-kit parse saved-page.mhtml -o saved-page.md --tier flash

docs.title: Default selection
docs.text:
• mineru-kit parse and local Python parse() default to Standard for PDFs.
  • After discovering service capabilities, the document library prefers Standard, then Basic for PDF/images. If neither is available, it returns quality_tier_unavailable rather than silently choosing Flash or uploading to the official service.
  • Tasks and Gradio share the Standard → Basic → Flash → Advanced preference, selecting Advanced automatically only when it is the sole available tier. Advanced shares models with Standard rather than downloading separate Advanced weights; the service must enable Advanced to accept corresponding PDF/image requests.
  • Library read consumes cached results without starting a new parse. Without an explicit tier, it prefers cached Advanced, Standard, then Basic results.

The API startup --tier is a ceiling including itself and lower tiers; --tier standard does not enable Advanced. Omission or --tier auto recommends a ceiling from the effective backend and hardware, potentially calibrating ONNX at startup. HTTP requests without a tier choose Standard → Basic → Flash → Advanced. Native documents always use Flash, independently of the enabled PDF/image tiers. See Tasks for the full rules.

docs.title: Backends and engines
docs.text:
Environment Automatic small models Automatic VLM Apple Silicon / MPS Torch / MPS llama.cpp / Metal Windows x64, base package ONNX / DirectML or CPU when no Torch accelerator runtime is available llama.cpp Linux x86_64, base package ONNX / WebGPU or CPU when no Torch accelerator runtime is available llama.cpp Linux, accelerator and full Torch vLLM, otherwise installed LMDeploy Windows, accelerator and full Torch LMDeploy CPU environment ONNX / CPU llama.cpp

Automatic selection uses installed dependencies and available devices. An explicit choice with missing dependencies fails instead of silently selecting another backend. model.onnx_device=auto|cpu|gpu controls ONNX devices independently of the VLM. MINERU_MODEL_ONNX_DEVICE overrides file configuration without persisting the override.

The 4.1 base package installs DirectML on Windows x64 and the Vulkan-backed WebGPU plugin on Linux x86_64. Compatible, confirmed discrete GPUs have priority. In auto mode, integrated or unclassified GPUs undergo applicable calibration; insufficient gains or unreliable execution select CPU. Linux uses CPU for older Intel/Xe-LP and unidentified Intel architectures, even with explicit gpu selection. Other systems, unavailable GPUs, or initialization failures log CPU fallback reasons.

Valid automatic choices can be saved to configuration. Set model.onnx_device back to auto and restart to recalibrate. Hardware changes invalidate old performance evidence; explicit or saved cpu choices are not overwritten when a discrete GPU is later connected. First calibration may download the recognition model; hardware info does not trigger it.

ONNX layout, OCR recognition, MFR, and UNet share device selection. Ordinary OCR detection uses CPU on Windows and may use WebGPU on Linux; seal detection, table classification, and SLANet Plus use CPU. GPU MFR handles full batches of eight, with remaining tails on CPU. The old MINERU_TABLE_DEVICE does not override ONNX UNet; Torch table models retain their CPU/CUDA policy. This ONNX path does not require manually replacing the runtime with onnxruntime-gpu.

Intel XPU is excluded from automatic LMDeploy selection. Linux prefers an installed XPU-compatible vLLM and otherwise falls back to llama.cpp; Windows uses llama.cpp.

model:
  small_backend: auto
  onnx_device: auto
  vlm:
    engine: auto

small_backend accepts auto/onnx/torch; engine accepts auto/llama-cpp/vllm/lmdeploy/mlx. macOS defaults to llama.cpp.

mineru-kit hardware detect --json
mineru-kit hardware info --json

detect shares API startup recommendations and may perform applicable ONNX calibration. info reads hardware, installed runtimes, effective configuration, and calibration records without benchmarking, downloading weights, or writing configuration.

Automatic API/WebUI tiers use the small-model backend’s device decision: GPU enables all four tiers; CPU with at least 12 available logical cores enables up to Standard, 4–11 cores up to Basic, and fewer than 4 cores only Flash. Recommendations do not query GPU memory capacity. Standard is the default request tier when available; CPU does not automatically enable Advanced. An explicit startup ceiling bypasses automatic recommendation.

docs.title: Resources and platform boundaries
docs.text:
Native text parsing needs no inference models. Basic can run on CPU. Standard / Advanced speed and memory depend on the VLM engine, input size, and concurrency. Plan for at least 16 GB of system memory for higher-throughput local deployment. NVIDIA deployments also need an engine-supported GPU, driver, and sufficient free VRAM; 8 GB is only a planning starting point, not a guarantee for every workload.

For Apple Silicon, at least 16 GB of unified memory and a direct macOS installation are recommended. The 4.1 Windows/Linux ONNX path supports compatible Intel, AMD, and NVIDIA GPUs; legacy vendor-accelerator guides remain scoped to MinerU <4.

See extension modules for installation and Model Source for downloads and configuration.

docs.title: 文档与推理
docs.text:
DocVortex 拥有原生格式解析、PDF 基础访问、schema、确定性后处理、素材、七种通用 renderer 与导出。 MinerU 拥有 OCR/VLM/Hybrid、模型生命周期、可选 LLM 增强、tier 策略、CLI/API/Gradio/Doclib，以及 Content List V1/V2。 依赖单向从 MinerU 指向 DocVortex 的公开接口。

MinerUParser 准备本地输入并调用 backend/analyze.py 的统一同步／异步门面。 原生格式进入 DocVortex；PDF 按 effort 与 parse_mode 选择原生或推理路径。 确定性后处理形成 MiddleJson 后才执行 MinerU 可选增强。ModelJson 只用于内部分析。

docs.title: 两类服务
docs.text:
服务 入口 状态范围 V1 API Server mineru/parser/api_server.py、mineru/tasks/ 上传、逐文件执行、结果 Files、租约；任务和索引在当前进程内 Router mineru/kit/router/ worker 发现、认证、调度、公共 ID 映射、源缓存与结果租约 file-parse mineru/kit/file_parse/ SQLite 保存 request_id 及上游引用，支持有条件恢复 Doclib server mineru/doclib/app.py、server.py、client.py 本地文档身份、路径、解析缓存、索引和运行时设置

V1 与 Doclib HTTP 接口不是同一协议。Doclib 使用 /api/v1，客户端通过 endpoint 文件发现 UDS 或 loopback TCP。 文件类型、请求默认档位和缓存读取的选择规则见 档位。

docs.title: Doclib 服务分工
docs.text:
模块 责任 services/ingest_svc.py 路径入库、源内容身份与基础信息 services/parse_queue_svc.py 请求校验、缓存覆盖与排队 services/parse_execution_svc.py 调用解析后端、保存产物并更新索引 services/content_read_svc.py 缓存读取、locator、分页内容与导出 background/ 入库、解析、扫描、watch、compaction、健康检测和 telemetry flush core/middle_json.py 已持久化历史 Middle JSON 的唯一兼容读取边界

缓存保存 Middle JSON 和需要的 sidecar，内容读取按需渲染。 Doclib 图像读取可在源文件仍可访问时按定位信息生成图像；这不意味着通用 ParseResult 持有源 PDF 对象。 read 不自动新建解析。缓存协议、索引和几何变更需验证实际读取及导出结果。

docs.title: 配置和生命周期
docs.text:
启动配置按 配置优先级 读取；Doclib 运行时 KV 和规则存储在 SQLite。 AppState 持有服务实例，跨实例配置显式传入。只有获得所属资源的实例才负责释放。 上传截止、执行状态、结果保留、下载活动引用和取消各有独立生命周期；取消后迟到结果不能改写终态。

公开错误按 接口边界 处理。没有远端许可时，不以错误恢复为由上传文档。 未完成设计集中在 待办，历史过程记录保存在仓库档案。

docs.text:
mineru parse → DoclibClient → doclib server
  → IngestService / ParseQueueService
  → ParseWorkerPool → ParseExecutionService
  → 本地 Flash，或配置的 managed / self-hosted / remote API
  → 缓存 Middle JSON 与素材 → ContentReadService → 阅读与导出

Doclib cache hit、覆盖计算、读取和 compaction 统一通过 core/middle_json.py 的历史缓存边界。 自托管状态和配置由 AppState 持有，不通过模块级隐式状态传递。

docs.title: 无状态解析与 Tasks 调用链
docs.text:
mineru-kit parse / Python parse → MinerUParser → doc_analyze
  → backend.analysis → DocVortex 原生能力或 MinerU OCR/VLM/Hybrid
  → DocVortex 确定性后处理 → MinerU 可选 LLM 增强 → ParseResult

HTTP / WebUI → Tasks → 执行后端 → 同一解析门面
  → task_outputs 多格式打包 → Files 下载

原始 ModelJson 仅服务分析和后处理，不进入公开结果包。 公开协议见 Tasks、Middle JSON； 后续工作见 待办，长期选择见 ADR。

docs.title: 配置体系
docs.text:
页码规范与历史结果兼容说明见 PDF 页码范围规范。

状态: Draft 读者: 想了解 doclib / mineru 配置的用户、实现配置能力的核心开发者 范围: 本地配置、远端配置、解析参数、环境变量和优先级规则 非目标: 替代 CLI 参数手册；替代部署文档 来源: 配置专题文档仍待继续核对

docs.title: 1. 定位
docs.text:
ONNX 小模型新增 model.onnx_device: auto | cpu | gpu，环境变量为 MINERU_MODEL_ONNX_DEVICE。首次实际使用时自动选择并保存，独显优先； 集显测速、重新选择及 DirectML 厂商预设见 ONNX 设备选择。

配置体系定义 MinerU 如何在不同启动阶段得到最终行为。

MinerU 有两类配置：

  • 启动前配置：doclib server 启动之前就必须知道，通常来自文件形式的配置或内置默认值。
  • 运行时配置：doclib server 启动之后可从 SQLite 读取和修改，由 config、watches、exclude_rules、parsing_rules 等表承载。

启动前还存在一个 bootstrap 根目录:

  • MINERU_HOME 决定 MinerU home，默认 ~/.mineru。
  • 默认配置文件路径是 $MINERU_HOME/config.yaml。
  • 默认 DB、日志和 UDS socket 从 MINERU_HOME 派生；默认 data_dir 是 $MINERU_HOME/doclib，其下包含 parsed/ 和 temp/。
  • MINERU_CONFIG 仍可显式指定配置文件路径；MINERU_HOME 只影响默认 home 和默认配置文件位置。

Python 模块导入不装载启动配置。默认调用路径使用 get_config()：第一次访问时读取 文件和环境并校验，之后复用进程默认配置；配置文件路径、存在状态和字段来源查询也使用 同一份首次装载结果。环境和文件变更不会自动刷新这份配置。

from mineru.config import get_config, load_config

settings = get_config()  # 读取并缓存进程默认配置
loaded = load_config()  # 按当前环境独立装载，不替换进程默认配置

原来的模块级 config 实例已移除，内部调用统一使用显式访问函数。load_config() 返回配置对象及其来源信息；Config() 只构造模型默认值，不读取 YAML 或应用环境覆盖。 依赖 MINERU_HOME 的默认路径在每次构造对象时解析。Doclib 的 create_app(cfg) 会保存传入配置的独立副本，并使用其中的全局日志级别补全服务日志设置。

docs.title: 远程 VLM
docs.text:
model.vlm 是所有本地解析入口的 VLM 默认配置，适用于 API server、Python parse() / parse_async() 和 mineru-kit parse。Standard/Advanced 将 VLM 推理交给 远程 MinerU OpenAI-compatible 服务，本地继续执行 Hybrid 处理；Flash/Basic 不调用远程 VLM。 上游须部署支持 MinerU 文档理解输出的模型，并提供 /v1/models 和 /v1/chat/completions。

model:
  vlm:
    server_url: http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1
    api_key: ${VLM_API_KEY:-}
    model: ""
    http_timeout: 600
    max_concurrency: 100

未配置 server_url 或显式设为空字符串时使用本地 VLM。地址可使用 HTTP/HTTPS 服务根地址或以 /v1 结尾的地址；反向代理前缀会保留，例如 https://host/proxy/v1 对应 https://host/proxy/v1/chat/completions。URL 不接受内嵌用户名、密码、query 或 fragment。 api_key 可为空；model 为空时要求上游模型列表恰好包含一个模型，多模型服务须显式指定模型名。 显式模型名也会通过模型列表校验。http_timeout 单位为秒，max_concurrency 是 VLM 推理请求并发，两者均为正整数；API 的 --concurrency 则控制解析任务并发。

环境变量包括 MINERU_MODEL_VLM_SERVER_URL、MINERU_MODEL_VLM_API_KEY、 MINERU_MODEL_VLM_MODEL、MINERU_MODEL_VLM_HTTP_TIMEOUT 和 MINERU_MODEL_VLM_MAX_CONCURRENCY。API 启动时的优先级为：显式启动参数 > 环境变量 > YAML > 默认值。启动参数及示例见 api-server。

Python 的 create_app()、MinerUParser、parse() / parse_async() 以及底层分析入口 可传入 vlm_config: VlmConfig | None：None 使用全局设置；显式对象完整覆盖全局设置。 应用与解析器各自保存配置副本，不修改全局配置或进程环境。

from mineru.config import VlmConfig
from mineru.parser import parse

result = parse("document.pdf", tier="standard")  # 使用全局 model.vlm
local_result = parse("document.pdf", vlm_config=VlmConfig())  # 本次使用本地 VLM

远程模式不会自动回退本地 VLM。旧底层环境变量 MINERU_VL_API_KEY、 MINERU_VL_MODEL_NAME 若与有效的新配置冲突，会明确报错；应清除旧变量并使用上述 MINERU_MODEL_VLM_* 配置。未配置远程地址时，旧 MINERU_VL_SERVER 不会启用远程 VLM。

Markdown render 同样读取启动前 config.yaml，当前支持以下配置：

render:
  latex_delimiters:
    display:
      left: "$$"
      right: "$$"
    inline:
      left: "$"
      right: "$"

四个 delimiter 必须为非空字符串。缺省值如上；环境变量可按现有字段路径规则覆盖， 例如 MINERU_RENDER_LATEX_DELIMITERS_INLINE_LEFT。

PDF 的 LLM 辅助后处理同样读取启动前 config.yaml：

llm_aided:
  api_key: ${MINERU_LLM_API_KEY:-}
  base_url: https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1
  model: qwen3.5-plus
  enable_thinking: false
  max_concurrency: 16
  features:
    title_leveling: false
    cross_page_table_cell_merge: false

两个功能默认关闭并共享同一套 OpenAI-compatible 连接参数。title_leveling 在严格 MiddleJson.pages 上优化标题层级，但只在 MiddleJson.is_full_document=true 的整本 PDF 输入中运行； 抽页结果会跳过标题优化。cross_page_table_cell_merge 不受整本输入限制，只消费确定性后处理 已经写入的 continues_prev，再把逐单元格的 0/1 结果写入后表根块 cell_merge。两个功能 通过同一个异步客户端并发请求，max_concurrency 是不小于 1 的共享请求上限，默认值为 16。 标题分级结果允许 1 到 6，段落标题的 1 会归一为 2，最终严格标题层级范围为 2 到 6。前置 MinerU VLM 的跨页单元格检测保持关闭。任一功能启用时，api_key、base_url 和 model 均必须为非空字符串；省略 enable_thinking 时不会发送该扩展参数。

环境变量可覆盖任意强类型字段，例如 MINERU_LLM_AIDED_API_KEY、 MINERU_LLM_AIDED_MAX_CONCURRENCY、 MINERU_LLM_AIDED_FEATURES_TITLE_LEVELING 和 MINERU_LLM_AIDED_FEATURES_CROSS_PAGE_TABLE_CELL_MERGE。

配置必须服务两个产品原则：

  • 隐私优先：任何配置都不能导致静默上传文档。
  • 质量优先：PDF/image 主动阅读未指定 tier 时使用默认选择策略，不能静默降级到 flash；OFD/EPUB/Office/HTML/MHTML/CSV/TSV 按实际能力归一为 flash；其它 text 直接读取。

全局日志级别由 log.level 控制，默认 info，可选 trace、debug、info、 warning、error、critical。环境变量 MINERU_LOG_LEVEL 可覆盖 YAML； 该配置作用于当前进程的 Loguru 默认 stderr sink，不会移除宿主程序显式添加的 自定义 sink。doclib.log.level 是 Doclib 进程日志级别的局部覆盖；api-server 启动参数 --log-level 是服务侧（Uvicorn/HTTP 访问/服务自身 stdlib 日志）的局部 覆盖，不影响 Loguru 默认 sink。

docs.title: 2.1 启动前配置
docs.text:
启动前配置解决“server 还没起来，不能读数据库”的问题。

这类配置包括：
